title: QBR modular slide bank + renewal tracker (smb + enterprise) - draft
content:
Purpose:
This is a working modular slide bank + lightweight renewal tracker and playbook intended to support CSMs running quarterly business reviews across both SMB and Enterprise accounts. Goal: make it trivial to assemble a 20–30 minute QBR tailored to account segment, surface renewal/expansion signals, and provide an actionable countdown playbook for renewals.

How to use this doc:
- Pick modules (A–G) appropriate to the customer tier and objectives.
- Use the SMB condensed flow (fast, product-led metrics + roadmap highlights) for accounts <$50k ARR.
- Use the Enterprise flow for strategic accounts: add exec summary, ROI, risk profile, and legal/contract timeline slides.
- Update the renewal tracker table per account at least 8 weeks prior to renewal.

Slide module bank (pick & assemble):
A. Cover + One-line outcome
- Title: QBR — <Customer Name> — <Quarter / Date>
- Intent: Set expectations, state success metric for the meeting (e.g., reduce inference cost by 25% / deploy to prod).
- Speaker notes: 30s intro, agenda, remind SLAs/recap partnership intent.

B. Agenda & Ask
- Bullets: 1) What we shipped, 2) Health + usage trends, 3) Roadmap & opportunities, 4) Risks + blockers, 5) Success plan / action items
- Intent: Align time and desired outcome (decision, follow-up workshop, renewal alignment).

C. Executive Summary (Enterprise only)
- One-slide snapshot: ARR, YOY growth, Net retention, Key wins, Primary ask (e.g., contract renewal / expansion).
- Data sources: billing, product analytics, customer success health score.
- Speaker notes: Lead with topline ROI and business impact. 2–3 minutes.

D. Usage & Health (modular charts)
- Charts included (modular): daily active endpoints, tokens / inference minutes by model, latency p95, error rate, cost per 1k tokens.
- Intent: surface meaningful trends and anomalies.
- Speaker notes: Highlight what changed since last QBR and why.

E. Adoption / Value Stories
- Bullets: Top 3 customer teams using the product, 2 short success stories (1 sentence each), quotes / support snippets.
- Tips: Ask for customer-sourced outcomes (ask customer to prepare a 30s win).

F. Roadmap alignment & product feedback
- Modular chunks: short-term (next 30 days), mid (90 days), long-term (6–12 months).
- Enterprise addition: compliance & private-deploy timeline if relevant.
- Speaker notes: Use this slide to request product reviews / beta participants.

G. Risk & Mitigation / Open blockers
- Template: Risk description, probability (low/med/high), impact (ops/revenue), mitigation owner + ETA.
- Speaker notes: Be candid; propose a single next-step per item.

H. Renewal & Expansion Plan (combined slide)
- Fields: Current ARR, Renewal date, Contract type, Renewal owner (AE/CSM), Suggested motion (upsell/renew/price change), Recommended next touch.
- Enterprise addition: Timeline with legal and procurement milestones.

I. Action items & owners (closing slide)
- 4–6 prioritized actions, owners, due dates.
- Request meeting cadence for next quarter.

SMB condensed flow (20 min)
- Cover (1 min)
- Health & quick wins (6–8 min)
- Roadmap + requests (4 min)
- Renewal ask or NPS / feedback (3–4 min)
- Wrap / action items (2 min)

Enterprise flow (35–45 min)
- Exec summary (3 min)
- Deep-dive on health + ROI (10–12 min)
- Roadmap & compliance items (8–10 min)
- Risk & mitigation (5–8 min)
- Commercial discussion (renewal/expansion) (6–8 min)
- Close & next steps (2–3 min)

Lightweight renewal tracker (table template — paste into CSM trackers/spreadsheet)
- Header row: Account | CSM | AE | Current ARR | Renewal date | Contract end | Renewal owner | Renewal status | Risk level | Last touch | Next action | Notes
- Sample row (text): Acme Corp | Maya H. | Connor B. | $185,000 | 2025-11-15 | 2025-11-30 | Connor B. | At risk | High | 2025-08-10 | Schedule pricing workshop | Procurement review underway; legal clause on data residency

Risk level definitions (use in tracker):
- Green: On track, renewal owner confirmed, no open blockers
- Yellow: 1–2 open items (procurement, non-critical product limits), CSM + AE engaged
- Red: Critical blocker (SLA miss, security, budget), exec escalation needed

Renewal playbook (8–12 week countdown)
- Week -12: Confirm renewal date, billing owner, and legal stakeholders. Draft QBR materials.
- Week -10: Run health deep-dive, identify friction points. Schedule executive touchpoint if Enterprise.
- Week -8: Present draft commercial proposal to AE; align on upsell options and pricing bands.
- Week -6: Deliver QBR + commercial proposal; capture objections and procurement needs.
- Week -4: Follow-up on legal and procurement items; escalate to sales leadership if red risk.
- Week -2: Finalize SOW/amendment; coordinate signatures and billing changes.
- Week 0: Renewal effective date — confirm go-live of any negotiated changes and update trackers.

Stakeholders & roles (recommended)
- CSM: owner of health narrative, running QBR, tracking product issues
- AE: commercial owner, pricing negotiations
- Solutions/SE: technical runbook + POC support for enterprise demos
- Legal/Finance: contract amendments and billing terms
- Product: input on roadmap, dependency ETA

Communication templates (short snippets — copy/paste)
- Save-the-date (to customer): "Hi <Name>, would love to schedule a 30–45 minute QBR during week of <date> to review outcomes and align on next quarter. Proposed agenda attached. Please let me know a few times that work."
- Post-QBR summary (to internal): "QBR complete for <Account>. Top outcomes: X, Y. Renewal status: <status>. Actions: <owner> to <action> by <date>. See tracker: <link>."

Common objections + suggested CS responses
- Objection: "We need lower cost per token."
  Response: Present Optimize recommendations (batching, q8 quant profile, model variant) and propose a 2-week pilot to measure 15–25% cost improvement.
- Objection: "We need on-prem / VPC deployment for compliance."
  Response: Surface Redwood Private timeline, list required security controls, open intake ticket to Security for pre-approval.

Data sources & preparation checklist (what to pull before QBR)
- Billing/export: last 12 months ARR movement and invoices
- Product analytics: tokens, endpoints, latency p95/p99, error rates, model versions used
- Support: P1/P2 incidents in past quarter, resolution status
- Evals/quality: any regressions detected by Optimize or eval harness
- Customer inputs: 2–3 internal stakeholders provide wins to share (ask at least 1 week ahead)

Internal pre-QBR runbook (CSM checklist)
- 14 days prior: Assemble slide modules, validate metrics, confirm AE alignment
- 7 days prior: Dry run with AE/SE (15–20 min), update slide deck with notes
- 3 days prior: Share final slide deck with attendee list and slide permissions for execs
- Day of: arrive 10 min early, confirm recording, capture action items in shared doc

Escalation play (when renewal risk = Red)
- Immediately: notify Sales Director and VP CS 
- Within 48 hours: schedule leadership-only sync to create mitigation plan (pricing concession, technical remediation timeline)
- 1 week: present mitigation plan to customer executive sponsor

Notes to self / open TODOs (draft nature)
- Add a one-slide ROI calc template with easy hooks to billing figures (TODO: derive formula w/ finance).
- Build a Google Sheets template that mirrors the tracker table to allow roll-up by CS Ops (TODO: CS Ops ticket).
- Create a short recording walkthrough of the deck for new CSM hires (TODO: recorded by Priya).

Appendix (useful snippets)
- Short agenda for 30 min executive QBR: Exec summary (3), ROI snapshot (5), Top 2 risks (7), Ask / next steps (5), Q&A (10)
- Sample NPS / CSAT slide blurb: 3–4 bullets with verbatim customer quotes

References & links
- Confluence: CS QBR templates (internal) — confluence:CS-QBR-templates-7890
- Jira: CS renewal tasks board — jira:CS-4121
- Slack: #cs-qbr for questions and dry-run invites
